And Marcher, with a sharp chill of fear. <break time="0.8s" /> Realized that she might die. <break time="0.8s" /> Before the Beast appeared. <break time="0.8s" /> What troubled him most. <break time="0.8s" /> Was not the thought of losing her. <break time="0.8s" /> But the fear that she would miss. <break time="0.8s" /> The end of their long watch. <break time="0.8s" /> As if a spectator should leave. <break time="0.8s" /> Just before the curtain fell. <break time="0.8s" /> Watching her closely. <break time="0.8s" /> He came to suspect. <break time="0.8s" /> That she had already guessed. <break time="0.8s" /> The nature of his fate. <break time="0.8s" /> And one evening he begged her. <break time="0.8s" /> To tell him whether she knew. <break time="0.8s" /> Something that he did not. <break time="0.8s" /> Her answer, gentle but firm. <break time="0.8s" /> Was that she would never tell him. <break time="0.8s" /> And her eyes. <break time="0.8s" /> Resting on him with infinite patience. <break time="0.8s" /> Seemed to hold a knowledge. <break time="0.8s" /> That was almost too painful to bear. <break time="0.8s" /> For the first time. <break time="0.8s" /> Marcher was haunted. <break time="0.8s" /> By a new and sharper dread. <break time="0.8s" /> Namely that the great event. <break time="0.8s" /> Might never come at all. <break time="0.8s" /> And that his long watch. <break time="0.8s" /> Might end in nothing. <break time="0.8s" /> One April evening. <break time="0.8s" /> He came to her house. <break time="0.8s" /> And found her sitting very still. <break time="0.8s" /> Dressed with unusual care. <break time="0.8s" /> So pale and composed. <break time="0.8s" /> That she seemed less a sick woman. <break time="0.8s" /> Than a serene and impenetrable sphinx. <break time="0.8s" /> As they talked once more. <break time="0.8s" /> Of the thing that was to come. <break time="0.8s" /> She said to him softly. <break time="0.8s" /> With a strange brightness in her face. <break time="0.8s" /> It is never too late.
